name: Tupac Shakur
description:
'''Tupac Amaru Shakur''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|uː|p|ɑː|k|_|ʃ|ə|ˈ|k|ʊər|audio=En-us-Tupac Shakur.wav}} {{respell|TOO|pahk|_|shə|KOOR}}; [[Andean Spanish|Spanish]]: ''Túpac''; June 16, 1971 – September 13, 1996),{{efn|name=Parish1}} also known by his stage names '''2Pac''' and '''Makaveli''', was an American rapper and actor. Shakur is regarded as one of the greatest and most influential rappers of all time{{efn|name=Reputation|Shakur has been described as one of the greatest rappers of all time in ''[[The New York Times]]''<ref name="Pearce2023">{{cite news |last=Pearce |first=Sheldon |date=October 21, 2023 |title=Tupac Shakur's Volatile Life, Delivered by Friendly Hands |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/10/21/books/review/tupac-shakur-authorized-biography-staci-robinson.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |department=Book Review |url-access=subscription |quote=Often hailed as one of the greatest rappers of all time |access-date=October 5, 2026}}</ref> and ''[[El País]]'',<ref name="Martinez2026">{{cite news |last=Martínez |first=Alonso |date=August 21, 2026 |title=Why is a man being tried for the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur 30 years after his death? |url=https://english.elpais.com/usa/2026-08-21/why-is-a-man-being-tried-for-the-murder-of-rapper-tupac-shakur-30-years-after-his-death.html |work=[[El País]] |quote=considered one of the greatest of all time |access-date=October 5, 2026}}</ref> and as one of the most influential by ''El País'',<ref name="Martinez2026"/> [[BBC News]],<ref name="Pandey2023">{{cite news |last=Pandey |first=Manish |date=September 29, 2023 |title=Tupac Shakur: Who was the rapper? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-66940018 |work=[[BBC News]] |department=Newsbeat |quote=widely considered to be one of the most influential and successful rappers of all-time |access-date=October 5, 2026}}</ref> the [[Associated Press]],<ref name="HillLandrum2026">{{cite news |last1=Hill |first1=Jessica |last2=Landrum |first2=Jonathan Jr. |date=August 31, 2026 |title=Jury convicts a man of first-degree murder for the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur |url=https://apnews.com/article/tupac-shakur-trial-las-vegas-duane-davis-0b0b080d73f91cd122b6dd438e5bbb80 |work=[[Associated Press]] |quote=considered one of the most influential rappers of all time |access-date=October 5, 2026}}</ref> and [[Reuters]].<ref name="Reuters2026">{{cite news |last1=Stapleton |first1=Erica |last2=Gorman |first2=Steve |last3=Queen |first3=Jack |date=August 10, 2026 |title=Jury selection begins for ex-gang leader charged with Tupac Shakur's 1996 murder |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/trial-opens-ex-gang-leader-charged-with-tupac-shakurs-1996-murder-2026-08-10/ |work=[[Reuters]] |quote=one of rap's most commercially successful and influential artists |access-date=October 5, 2026}}.</ref>}} and has sold [[List of best-selling music artists|more than 75 million records]] worldwide. Some of Shakur's music addressed social injustice, political issues, and the marginalization of [[African Americans]], but he was also synonymous with [[gangsta rap]] and violent lyrics.

Shakur was born in [[New York City]] to parents who were [[Black Panther Party]] members. Raised by his mother, [[Afeni Shakur]], he relocated to the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] in 1988. His debut album ''[[2Pacalypse Now]]'' (1991) cemented him as a central figure in [[West Coast hip-hop]] for his [[political rap]] lyrics. Shakur achieved further critical and commercial success with his subsequent albums ''[[Strictly 4 My N.I.G.G.A.Z...]]'' (1993) and ''[[Me Against the World]]'' (1995). His [[RIAA certification|Diamond]]-certified album ''[[All Eyez on Me]]'' (1996), the first hip-hop [[double album]], abandoned introspective lyrics for volatile gangsta rap. It yielded two [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]-number one singles, "[[California Love]]" and "[[How Do U Want It]]". Alongside his solo career, Shakur formed the group [[Thug Life (group)|Thug Life]] and collaborated with artists like [[Snoop Dogg]], [[Dr. Dre]], and the [[Outlawz]]. As an actor, Shakur starred in the films ''[[Juice (1992 film)|Juice]]'' (1992), ''[[Poetic Justice (film)|Poetic Justice]]'' (1993), ''[[Above the Rim]]'' (1994), ''[[Bullet (1996 film)|Bullet]]'' (1996), ''[[Gridlock'd]]'' (1997), and ''[[Gang Related]]'' (1997).

In November 1994, Shakur was shot five times in the lobby of a New York recording studio and experienced legal troubles, including [[incarceration]]. He served eight months in prison on [[sexual abuse]] charges, but was released pending appeal in 1995. Following his release, he signed to [[Suge Knight|Marion "Suge" Knight]]'s label [[Death Row Records]] and became embroiled in the [[East Coast–West Coast hip-hop rivalry]], which included a high-profile feud with his former friend [[the Notorious B.I.G.]] On September 7, 1996, [[Murder of Tupac Shakur|Shakur was murdered]] by an unidentified assailant in a [[drive-by shooting]] in [[Paradise, Nevada]]; he died six days later. On August 31, 2026, [[South Side Compton Crips]] member Duane "Keffe D" Davis was convicted of orchestrating Shakur's murder, but the shooter (suspected to be [[Baby Lane]]) has not been conclusively identified.

Shakur's double-length posthumous album [[Greatest Hits (Tupac Shakur album)|''Greatest Hits'']] (1998) is one of his two releases—and one of only nine hip-hop albums—to have been certified Diamond in the United States. Five more albums have been released since Shakur's death, including the acclaimed ''[[The Don Killuminati: The 7 Day Theory]]'' (1996) under the stage name Makaveli, all of which have been certified multi-platinum in the United States. In 2002, Shakur was inducted into the [[Hip Hop Hall of Fame|Hip-Hop Hall of Fame]]. In 2017, he was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in his first year of eligibility. ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked Shakur among the [[Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Artists of All Time|100 Greatest Artists of All Time]]. In 2023, he was awarded a posthumous star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]]. His influence in music, activism, songwriting, and other areas of culture has been the subject of academic studies.
